title: Ankara Unveils 2027-2029 Economic Roadmap as Disinflation Stays Priority; CHP Purge and DEM Congress Reshape Opposition
subhead: Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz presented a new Medium-Term Program cutting the 2026 growth forecast to 3.3% and targeting 9% inflation by 2029, while the CHP's internal purge and the DEM Party's congress redraw Turkey's opposition landscape.

sections.heading: Economy: Ankara Cuts Growth Forecast, Keeps Disinflation as Top Priority
sections.body: Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz unveiled the new Medium-Term Program (MTP) for 2027-2029 on Sunday, keeping disinflation and price stability at the center of policy. The government revised its 2026 growth forecast down to 3.3% from an earlier 3.8% and expects inflation to end the year at 28.4%, according to Daily Sabah. Under the roadmap, inflation is projected to fall to 21% in 2027, 13.5% in 2028 and 9% in 2029. Yilmaz said the Middle East war had driven the upward revision of the inflation outlook, estimating the conflict's direct and indirect effects on inflation at roughly 7 percentage points per the central bank. Official data shows annual inflation eased to 31.51% in August from 31.75% in July.
sections.whyItMatters: The roadmap signals Ankara is betting on continued tight policy through the election cycle, but the war-driven inflation revision shows how much of Turkey's economic trajectory now hinges on external shocks beyond its control.

sections.heading: Domestic Politics: Kilicdaroglu's CHP Purge Heads Toward Sept. 9 Showdown
sections.body: The opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) is in the final stage of the internal overhaul pledged by Kemal Kilicdaroglu, who returned to the chairmanship vowing to eliminate 'thieves and bribe-takers through cleansing.' Daily Sabah reports that most lawmakers and mayors suspected of corruption have been referred to disciplinary boards or forced to resign and join the breakaway New Party (YP). Attention now turns to the party's delegate structure, with all eyes on Sept. 9, the party's founding anniversary, when Kilicdaroglu is expected to make major statements. Provincial and district leadership elections will be held and congress delegates determined from scratch. The purge follows bribery allegations that overshadowed the 2023 congress, in which Kilicdaroglu unexpectedly lost the chairmanship by a narrow margin amid claims that Ozgur Ozel and Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu bought delegate votes. In August, the CHP referred 49 members to disciplinary proceedings over alleged work for another party.
sections.whyItMatters: Kilicdaroglu's consolidation of the CHP and the split with Ozel's YP faction is redrawing Turkey's opposition ahead of the 2028 election, with the two camps now competing for the same anti-government vote.

sections.heading: Kurdish Politics: DEM Party Holds Congress, Weighs 'Third Way'
sections.body: The pro-Kurdish Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) held its congress on Sunday amid speculation of a significant overhaul. Co-chair Tulay Hatimogullari called the gathering a 'threshold where DEM will review its policies,' stressing the need for changes in the party's organization and political language, per Daily Sabah. Co-chair Tuncer Bakirhan said the party would remain a 'third way' in Turkey's political landscape. The congress comes as the Terror-Free Turkiye initiative — which produced a law deferring sentences for surrendered PKK members — has pushed the DEM Party toward closer ties with the ruling AK Party and MHP alliance, a notable shift for a party long aligned with PKK-linked positions.
sections.whyItMatters: The DEM Party's repositioning is a bellwether for the Kurdish peace process: whether it embraces the government's disarmament track or reverts to its traditional autonomy agenda will shape the stability of the southeast and the 2028 election math.

sections.heading: Infrastructure: Ankara Moves to Privatize Istanbul Bridges and Highways
sections.body: Turkey plans to sell 30-year operating rights for the July 15 Martyrs Bridge and the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge, along with several highways including the Nigde-Pozanti, Gaziantep Ring Motorway and Caglayan-Yenisehir routes, according to a presidential decree published in the Official Gazette. The Privatization Administration (OIB) stressed the move does not involve selling public assets — ownership stays with the state, with operating rights transferred for a set period, and the process to be completed by Dec. 31, 2031. Turkey first attempted to sell the bridges' operating rights more than a decade ago but balked at a winning $5.7 billion bid it deemed too low. The new decision extends the operating period to 30 years and allows privatization as a whole or in separate groups. Reports suggest Ankara is seeking to ease budget pressures.
sections.whyItMatters: The privatization push reflects the fiscal strain of the disinflation program — Ankara is monetizing state assets to relieve budget pressure without raising taxes ahead of elections.

sections.heading: Energy: Iraq Eyes Ceyhan Route as It Expands Exports Beyond Hormuz
sections.body: Iraq has lifted its crude export capacity to more than 3 million barrels per day since the start of September and aims for 5 million bpd, Oil Ministry official Khudair told the Iraqi News Agency, per Daily Sabah. Baghdad is advancing two strategic pipeline routes ordered by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi: a Basra-Haditha-Fish-Khabur northern route that would connect southern fields to the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline and Turkey's Mediterranean port of Ceyhan, and a western Haditha-Banias route to Syria's Mediterranean coast. The push comes as Iraq seeks to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz, which remains disrupted by the US-Iran conflict. Separately, OPEC+ kept its October output targets unchanged on Sunday, with the group still producing well below targets; Rystad Energy's Jorge Leon noted OPEC 'has very limited power over the physical oil market' as attention shifts to the 2027 baseline debate.
sections.whyItMatters: A revived Ceyhan corridor would restore Turkey's role as a key Mediterranean energy transit hub and deepen Ankara-Baghdad energy interdependence, while Hormuz disruption keeps the strategic value of overland routes high.

sections.heading: TRNC: Girne Ferry Disaster Rescue Continues as Turkey Deploys Assets
sections.body: Turkey is supporting the search-and-rescue operation after the high-speed passenger vessel Filo Jet sank off Girne (Kyrenia) in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. The ship, operating between Girne and Tasucu Port in Mersin, began taking on water shortly after departing around noon on Aug. 30 and sank while trying to return. TRNC Prime Minister Unal Ustel said the vessel carried 267 passengers and crew; 239 were rescued, the bodies of 13 recovered, and search efforts continued for 15 missing. Turkey has deployed seven helicopters, aircraft, UAVs, vessels and boats, with SAT commandos and naval diving teams assisting. Psychosocial support teams from Turkey's Family and Social Services Ministry are meeting with passengers and relatives of the missing at Girne Port.
sections.whyItMatters: The disaster is a humanitarian and political test for Ankara's relationship with the TRNC, with Turkey's rapid deployment underscoring its role as the guarantor of the breakaway state.

sections.heading: Foreign Relations: Armenian Patriarch Prays for Rapprochement; Eygi Justice Still Elusive
sections.body: Armenian Orthodox Patriarch Sahak Masalyan led a service at the historic Akdamar Church on Lake Van on Sunday, praying for the restoration of Turkish-Armenian ties and saying 'people living in these lands deserve peace.' Daily Sabah notes Turkey and Armenia took major steps toward rapprochement this year, including a visit to Yerevan by Vice President Yilmaz. Separately, the family of Aysenur Ezgi Eygi, the 26-year-old Turkish-American activist killed in the West Bank in 2024, said justice remains elusive two years on — the US has not opened an independent investigation despite a Washington Post finding that she was shot about 20 minutes after clashes had ended, deferring instead to an Israeli inquiry that has produced no public finding.
sections.whyItMatters: The Akdamar service signals the normalization track with Armenia is advancing quietly, while the unresolved Eygi case remains a live irritant in Turkey's relations with both Washington and Israel.

bottomLine: Ankara's new 2027-2029 Medium-Term Program is the day's defining development: the government is holding the line on disinflation — targeting 9% inflation by 2029 — even as it cuts the 2026 growth forecast to 3.3% and blames the Middle East war for roughly 7 points of the inflation overshoot. Domestically, the opposition is being reshaped from within: Kilicdaroglu's CHP purge heads toward a Sept. 9 climax while the DEM Party's congress weighs whether to embrace the government's Kurdish peace track. The privatization of Istanbul's bridges and Iraq's push to route more crude through Ceyhan both point to the fiscal and energy pressures shaping Turkey's choices. The Girne ferry disaster and the unresolved Eygi case round out a day heavy on domestic consolidation and quiet foreign-policy maneuvering.
sources: Daily Sabah (MTP/economic roadmap, CHP overhaul, DEM Party congress, Istanbul bridges privatization, Iraq oil exports, OPEC+, Girne ferry disaster, Armenian patriarch, Eygi justice, AK Party poll)
